procs.rm: Roundwood logs (eucalyptus, hardwood mix), bamboo (where used)
procs.q: Chip size distribution, bark%, dirt content, moisture%, fines%

loc: Chip pile reclaimer to digester feed conveyor (final quality checkpoint before cooking)
d: Analyses overhead camera feeds at the digester feed (size, bark%, dirt, fines).
Detects oversize chips, fines, bark contamination and dirt entering the digester.
Provides real-time chip quality feedback for chipper adjustment and blending decisions.
Uses existing inline metal detectors for foreign-material trip (no new metal detection added).
p: Chip quality variability causes digester kappa swings
Lab chip analysis slow (4-8 hr lag) — too slow for blending decisions
Manual visual inspection of chip pile is incomplete
Yield loss from oversize/fines not tracked in real-time

loc: Log-to-debarker conveyor (heavy abrasive logs, jamming risk)
Chip pile reclaimer to digester feed trunk belts (single-point failure for digester)
Foreign material detection at digester feed (metal in chips damages digester feed system)
d: Analyses camera images of belt surfaces, vibration on idlers and metal detector signals.
Detects belt tears, mis-tracking, foreign material and bearing degradation.
Provides location-tagged alerts before catastrophic belt failure or downstream damage.
p: Long wood yard conveyors fail with limited warning
Foreign material in chips damages digester feed system
Belt damage often noticed only on inspection rounds
Manual belt inspection cannot cover 24/7 operation

procs.out: Brown stock pulp, weak black liquor (15% solids), TRS gases
procs.q: Kappa number, yield%, viscosity (mPa.s), soda losses, brightness post-wash

d: Analyses chip-meter data, cooking liquor flow and temperature, and H-factor (no online kappa; kappa is measured offline and manually in the lab).
Models cooking kinetics and predicts blow-line kappa, yield and pulp strength from H-factor and liquor charge.
Advises on liquor charge, active alkali, cooking temperature and chip retention to balance pulp quality (target kappa), utility cost (steam, white liquor, waste-heat recovery) and throughput.
p: Kappa measured offline in lab (2-4 hr lag); no online analyzer for real-time control
Cooking parameters set on operator experience; H-factor not used as a live control lever
AA charge often over-dosed (operator caution), raising chemical recovery cost
Utility cost (steam, liquor, waste heat) per tonne not optimized against quality and throughput

procs.out: Brown stock pulp, weak black liquor (15% solids), TRS gases
procs.q: Kappa number, yield%, viscosity (mPa.s), soda losses, brightness post-wash

uc.t: Batch / RDH Digester H-Factor & Utility Cost Advisory
d: Analyses per-cook temperature/pressure schedule, liquor charge, accumulator hot/warm liquor use and H-factor (kappa measured offline and manually per batch).
Models batch cooking kinetics and predicts end-of-cook kappa and yield from H-factor and charge.

Advises on cook schedule, AA charge and RDH liquor displacement to hit target kappa while minimising fresh steam (maximising warm/hot liquor and waste-heat reuse) and protecting batch-to-batch consistency.
p: Batch-to-batch kappa variability with offline lab kappa only
RDH liquor displacement / accumulator use not optimised for steam economy
Cook schedule set on experience; H-factor not used as a live target
Fresh steam over-used where warm/hot liquor or waste heat could substitute
kpi: H-factor per batch and batch-to-batch kappa consistency

procs.rm: Brown stock pulp slurry, wash water (recycled hot)
procs.out: Washed brown stock pulp, weak black liquor to evaporators
procs.q: Wash loss (kg Na₂SO₄/ADt), dilution factor, drum speed, post-wash brightness (ISO%), dirt content, soda losses

d: Analyses conductivity, dilution factor, drum speed and wash water flow on each stage of the brown stock washers.
Predicts wash efficiency and soda losses; identifies anomalies in drum loading and felt blinding.
Builds a soft sensor for post-wash brown stock brightness at the final stage (between lab samples).
Advises on dilution factor, wash water distribution and drum speed across stages for minimum wash loss and stable post-wash brightness.
p: Wash loss varies across washer stages
Felt blinding reduces drum efficiency
Dilution factor manually set
Soda makeup cost higher than design
kpi: Washer drum loading and drum speed
Post-wash brightness (ISO%) — soft sensor vs lab

procs.out: Strong black liquor (65-75% solids), condensate, recovered soap
procs.q: BL solids%, Brix, dilution factor, scale buildup, steam economy (t steam/t water evaporated)

uc.t: Evaporator Scale, Cleaning & Steam Economy Optimization
d: Analyses heat transfer coefficient (U) trends per effect, soap recovery, liquor flow/temperature, vacuum levels, condensate quality and steam consumption.
Predicts scale buildup rates and remaining time-to-clean for each evaporator body, and detects steam economy degradation, vacuum issues and sub-optimal liquor flow splits.
Provides cleaning schedule optimization plus advisory on liquor flow distribution and operating setpoints to maximise steam economy and uptime.
p: Evaporator scaling reduces steam economy 15-20% before cleaning
Cleaning schedules reactive, not predictive; mechanical cleaning takes 8-24 hr downtime
Steam economy degrades silently; vacuum issues hidden until production drop
Liquor flow splits manually set; condensate flooding common in some effects
kpi: Heat transfer coefficient U per effect (W/m²K)
Overall steam economy (t evap / t steam)
Vacuum per effect and liquor flow distribution
Time-between-cleans (days) and cleaning frequency per year

procs.rm: Strong black liquor (65-75% solids), makeup Na₂SO₄, white liquor for ESP
procs.ut: Combustion air (primary, secondary, tertiary), ID/FD fans, soot blowers
procs.out: HP steam, smelt (Na₂CO₃ + Na₂S), flue gas, fly ash
procs.q: Steam generation rate, TRS, smelt bed temp, sulfidity recovery, NOx, char bed stability

d: Analyses BL solids, BL firing rate, primary/secondary/tertiary air distribution, char bed temperature, ESP O₂, TRS emissions and CO levels.
Models combustion kinetics and char bed dynamics; predicts steam generation, TRS emissions and bed stability windows.
Provides advisory on air distribution, BL spray pattern and load setpoints for maximum steam, minimum emissions, stable char bed.
p: RB is the most-stopped unit at Indian mills
Combustion air balance manually set
TRS excursions cause regulatory issues
Bed upsets cascade to major shutdowns (₹3-5 cr/event)

d: Analyses thermal and visual camera feeds of the char bed and smelt spouts in real time.
Detects bed instability, channel formation, smelt spout blockages and char bed shape anomalies.
Provides early warning to operators for corrective action before bed upsets escalate.
p: Bed instability often detected too late
Channel formation forces emergency response
Smelt spout blockages cause smelt overflow
Manual visual checks by operator are intermittent

d: Analyses heat transfer coefficient trends per section (gas-side temperature, steam temperature/pressure), time since last blow per individual blower, BL solids variability, and effectiveness history of each blower.
Predicts heat transfer degradation per zone and recommends optimal sequence and timing for each soot blower individually.
Provides demand-driven blowing schedule that maximizes heat recovery while minimizing soot-blowing steam consumption and tube erosion.
p: Soot blowing typically scheduled by time, not by actual fouling state
Operators over-blow as precaution (wastes HP steam at 3-5% of RB output)
Over-blowing erodes tubes and shortens campaign life
Under-blowing reduces boiler efficiency (lost steam generation)
kpi: Soot blowing steam consumption (t/h or t/d)
Heat transfer coefficient trend per zone
Tube erosion rate / campaign tube life

procs.rm: Lime mud (CaCO₃ from causticizing), makeup limestone
procs.out: Reburned lime (CaO) for causticizing, flue gas
procs.q: Lime activity (CaO available%), residual CaCO₃, fuel/lime ratio (GJ/t), ring formation, refractory wear

d: Analyses fuel firing rate, air ratio, kiln shell temperature profile, lime activity (CaO availability) and lime mud feed properties.
Models calcining kinetics and predicts lime quality, fuel consumption and ring formation tendency.
Provides advisory on fuel rate, air distribution and feed adjustment for target lime activity with minimum fuel.
p: Fuel cost rising; consumption higher than design
Lime activity varies batch to batch
Ring formation forces unplanned shutdowns
Refractory wear unpredictable

d: Analyses kiln shell IR scanner data, thermal camera feeds and refractory thickness models along the kiln length.
Detects shell hotspots indicating refractory thinning, spalling and localized wear.
Provides location-tagged alerts and predicts refractory campaign life remaining.
p: Refractory failure forces unplanned shutdowns
Manual shell temperature checks miss developing damage
Campaign timing reactive
Refractory replacement cost high

d: Analyses thermal camera feeds at the discharge end and calcining-zone temperature/shell profile.
Detects ring and ball formation in the calcining zone before discharge issues appear.
Provides early alerts and schedules ring removal to avoid forced shutdowns.
p: Ring formation hidden until discharge issues appear
Ring removal reactive and disruptive
Ball formation affects lime quality and throughput
Manual checks intermittent

procs.out: White liquor (NaOH + Na₂S), lime mud (CaCO₃) to lime kiln
procs.q: Causticizing efficiency (CE), reduction efficiency (RE), AA, TTA, lime grit

d: Analyses green liquor TTA, white liquor AA, lime ratio (CaO/TTA), causticizer agitator current and lime grit.
Predicts causticizing efficiency and white liquor strength versus lime addition rate.
Provides optimal lime addition setpoint to maximize CE without lime overdosing.
p: CE drifts; manual control by operators
Lime overdosing common (operator caution)
Reduced CE wastes lime kiln capacity
White liquor quality variable

procs.rm: Washed brown stock, ClO₂, O₂, H₂O₂, NaOH, H₂SO₄
procs.ut: Steam (tower heating), power (pumps, mixers), MP/LP steam
procs.q: Brightness (ISO%), viscosity (mPa.s), kappa stage-wise, strength, ClO₂/NaOH consumption (kg/t)

uc.t: Bleach Plant Optimization (Brightness, Inferential Sensing & Tower Mixing)
d: Analyses kappa before the bleach plant, incoming pulp brightness, ClO₂/alkali dosage per stage, tower temperatures, retention times, mixer power and pH/temperature profile.
Models bleaching kinetics and builds soft sensors for brightness and viscosity between lab samples (typically every 2 hours), and detects poor mixing, channeling and reaction non-uniformity.
Provides setpoint optimization for chemical charge, tower temperature and mixer setpoints to hit target brightness with minimum ClO₂ and NaOH and uniform stage-wise reaction.
p: ClO₂ (₹180/kg) often overdosed for safety margin; chemical cost per tonne above benchmark
Lab brightness lag (2 hr) prevents real-time control; operators wait for lab confirmation
Kappa variability upstream drives bleach demand swings
Poor mixing and channeling waste chemicals and create non-uniform brightness
kpi: ClO₂ consumption (kg/t pulp) and NaOH consumption (kg/t pulp)
Tower mixer power, pH variance and temperature uniformity

procs.rm: Bleached pulp, additives (sizing, fillers CaCO₃/TiO₂, retention aids), broke
procs.out: Furnish to headbox (target consistency, freeness, additive dosing)
procs.q: Freeness (CSF), consistency%, pH, conductivity, retention, drainage rate

uc.t: Stock Prep Refiner Plate Wear & Energy Optimization
d: Analyses refiner motor power, no-load power baseline, vibration on refiner shaft, freeness at refiner outlet and plate gap (where instrumented).
Predicts refiner plate wear, specific energy consumption (kWh/t) and impending plate clash events.
Provides plate change scheduling and advisory on refiner load distribution.
p: Refiner energy is major mill consumer
Plate clash damages refiner (₹10-20 lakh/event)
Plate life varies by furnish composition
Manual plate gap adjustment

d: Analyses inlet flow rates, freeness, ash content and strength of virgin pulp, recycled pulp and broke streams.
Models final furnish properties versus mix ratio and predicts paper machine runnability.
Provides optimal furnish ratio to balance cost, strength and runnability targets.
p: Furnish ratio not dynamically optimized
Broke management reactive
Quality vs cost tradeoffs not visible to operators
Strength variability from mix changes

d: Analyses approach flow consistency, cleaner pressure drops, screen amperages, deaerator vacuum and dosing flows.
Detects consistency drift, cleaner blockages and screen damage.
Provides advisory on dilution control, cleaner cleaning cycles and screen maintenance.
p: Consistency variability causes basis weight swings
Cleaner blockages cause downtime
Screen damage discovered post-failure
Approach flow disturbances cascade to wet end

procs.rm: Furnish from approach flow, sizing chemicals, fillers, retention aids
procs.ut: Steam (drying), power (vacuum, drives), compressed air, cooling water, fresh/recycled water
procs.out: Paper jumbo reel (target basis weight, moisture, brightness, smoothness)
procs.q: Basis weight (gsm), moisture%, caliper (μm), brightness, smoothness, formation, breaks/day, broke%

d: Analyses wet end conditions (consistency, retention, drainage), press section vacuum and load profiles, dryer section steam pressures, sheet tension and felt conductivity along the machine.
Models web break precursor patterns and predicts break risk in advance with location (wet end / press / dryer / reel).
Provides operator alerts with corrective actions to stabilize the sheet before the break occurs.
p: Web breaks cost ₹15-25 lakh per event
Typical 200-400 breaks/yr at 0.5 MTPA mill = ₹30-100 cr/yr
Breaks unpredictable; operator surprise events
Restart cycles waste steam, chemicals, time

d: Analyses high-speed line scan camera feeds across the full sheet width at the reel.
Detects holes, fish-eyes, dirt specks, wrinkles, fold marks, edge cracks and basis weight variations.
Provides defect classification, location-tagged alerts and CD/MD trend analysis for root cause investigation.
p: Defects often discovered post-production at customer
Customer rejects expensive (₹5,000-50,000/t)
Manual sampling insufficient
Defect root cause investigation slow

d: Analyses headbox slice profile, retention/drainage performance, fines/filler retention, vacuum levels and white water consistency.
Models wet end stability and predicts dewatering performance versus furnish properties and machine speed.
Provides advisory on retention aid dosing, dilution, slice profile and vacuum setpoints.
p: Wet end is upstream source of most PM problems
Retention aid overdosed for safety
Drainage variability impacts dryer load
Manual setpoint adjustment

uc.t: Dryer Section Energy & Moisture Profile Optimization
d: Analyses steam pressures across dryer groups, condensate flows, sheet moisture profile and dryer surface temperatures.
Models drying kinetics and predicts moisture profile versus steam distribution and machine speed.
Provides advisory on steam group setpoints for target moisture with minimum steam consumption.
p: Drying is largest steam consumer (₹600 cr/MTPA paper)
Steam group setpoints not optimized
Moisture profile variability causes broke
Operator adjustments based on experience only

d: Analyses scanner data for basis weight, moisture and caliper CD profiles, headbox dilution actuators, steam shower, and induction profilers (where available).
Models CD response to actuator changes and predicts steady-state profiles.
Provides advisory on actuator setpoints for tighter CD profiles and reduced 2σ.
p: CD profile variability forces higher basis weight buffer (cost)
Actuator coordination manual
Profile drift over shift
Quality at edges different from center

uc.t: Press Felt & Dryer Felt Condition Monitoring
d: Analyses camera images of felt surfaces, felt water content via NIR, dryer dewatering rate and press load profile.
Detects felt blinding, compaction, edge wear and damage patterns.
Provides felt cleaning and replacement scheduling to optimize felt life and dewatering performance.
p: Felts cost ₹10-30 lakh per set
Felt blinding gradual; hard to detect
Premature changes waste felt life
Late changes hurt dewatering and increase dryer steam

d: Analyses camera images at the reel and unwinder/winder of the finished roll.
Detects edge cracks, telescoping, wrinkles, surface defects and basis weight anomalies in roll structure.
Provides quality scoring and rejects bad rolls before customer dispatch.
p: Roll defects cause customer credits and returns
Manual roll inspection slow
Edge cracks discovered at customer
Reel structure issues hidden

procs.rm: Base paper, coating color (latex + pigments CaCO₃/kaolin + additives)
procs.out: Coated paper (target coat weight, smoothness, brightness)
procs.q: Coat weight (gsm/side), coverage, smoothness, brightness gain, defects (scratches/streaks)

d: Analyses coating color flow, blade pressure, machine speed, online coat weight gauge and brightness scanner data.
Models coating coverage versus operating parameters and predicts coat weight CD/MD profile.
Provides advisory on blade pressure, color flow and speed for target coverage with minimum chemical usage.
p: Coating color overdosed for coverage safety
Blade pressure manual setting
Coverage variability causes spec issues
Coat weight CD/MD profile drift

d: Analyses high-resolution line scan camera feeds of the coated surface post-drying.
Detects coating streaks, scratches, bare spots, picking and orange peel defects.
Provides defect classification with CD/MD location and triggers blade change or color adjustment advisories.
p: Coating defects expensive (coated grades are premium)
Streak/scratch from blade wear hidden until inspection
Bare spots cause customer rejects
Manual visual inspection slow

d: Analyses IR dryer power, steam dryer pressures, sheet moisture profile and base paper moisture entry.
Models drying versus coating chemistry and predicts dryer load for target moisture exit.
Provides drying setpoints for energy efficiency without quality loss.
p: IR drying expensive (electric power)
Drying setpoints conservative
Moisture variability affects quality
Energy consumption higher than design

procs.out: Customer rolls (slit, wound to target diameter and hardness)
procs.q: Roll hardness, edge condition, slit accuracy, taper, telescoping

uc.t: Winder Web Break & Roll Quality Optimization
d: Analyses winder tension profile, drum loading, knife condition, paper tension and unwinder behavior.
Predicts winder web breaks and roll structure defects (soft rolls, hard rolls, telescoping).
Provides operator alerts and tension/load setpoint advisory.
p: Winder breaks waste finished paper (expensive)
Roll hardness variability
Tension profile drift
Knife wear hidden

d: Analyses camera feeds of slit edges and side trim removal at the winder.
Detects edge cracks, ragged edges, slit knife wear and trim handling issues.
Provides knife change recommendations and quality alerts.
p: Edge cracks from slit knives cause rejects
Knife change scheduling reactive
Trim handling jams
Edge quality varies

uc.t: Integrated Multi-Feeder Coal Load Balancing + Bed Temperature Stabilization
d: Analyses individual coal feeder speeds/currents, bed temperature thermocouples across the furnace, primary/secondary air distribution, bed pressure and flue gas O₂/CO.
Models per-feeder fuel delivery vs local bed temperature and detects feeder imbalance, hot/cold spots, bed-temperature excursions and incipient agglomeration/clinkering.
Advises on per-feeder load balancing and air distribution to hold a uniform, stable bed temperature for consistent steam generation and minimum unburnt carbon.
p: Multiple coal feeders run unbalanced, creating bed hot/cold spots
Bed temperature excursions risk agglomeration/clinkering and forced derates
Variable fuel (coal + biomass + sludge) destabilises the bed
Air/fuel balance set manually; ash carbon higher than design
kpi: Feeder load balance / deviation across feeders
Bed temperature excursion events per month

uc.t: Plant-Wide RCA & Heat Rate Diagnostics Engine
d: Integrates boiler, turbine, steam-network and auxiliary data into a station heat-rate and energy-balance model spanning fuel-in to power/steam-out.
Continuously decomposes heat-rate deviation into attributable causes (boiler efficiency, condenser vacuum, auxiliary power, steam losses, fuel quality) and ranks contributors.
Provides guided root-cause analysis and prioritised corrective actions to recover heat rate and reduce specific energy across the utility island.
p: Heat-rate deviations not decomposed to attributable causes
RCA is manual, slow and inconsistent across engineers
Boiler/turbine/auxiliary losses analysed in silos
Fuel-quality and operating-mode effects not separated
kpi: Station heat rate (kCal/kWh) and deviation from best-achieved

uc.t: Energy Management System (Power, Compressed Air & Steam Monitoring)
d: Single plant-wide energy management layer monitoring electrical power, compressed air and steam across all generators and consumers.

Builds real-time energy balances (power kWh, compressed air Nm³, steam t/h), attributes consumption to areas/assets and detects leaks, failed steam traps, compressor cycling and inefficient consumers.
Provides cross-utility optimization advisory (load shifting, sequencing, pressure setpoints, demand attribution) and a unified specific-energy view (GJ/t paper).
p: Power, compressed air and steam monitored in silos (no unified EMS)
Steam balance and venting losses hidden from operators
Compressed air leaks and compressor cycling waste energy continuously
Consumption not attributed to areas/assets; demand forecasting manual
kpi: Specific energy (GJ/t paper) — power, air and steam combined
Compressed air specific energy (kWh/Nm³) and leak rate %
Steam balance, network pressure stability and vent losses

loc: HP/MP/LP steam header drip legs (prevent water hammer, drain condensate)
Paper machine dryer cylinder drains (largest steam consumer area)
Evaporator and digester process equipment drains
Distribution and tracing line drainage points across the mill
d: Analyses inlet and outlet temperature signatures from wireless battery-powered sensors deployed at each steam trap.
Detects failed-open (steam passing through), failed-closed (condensate backup), and failed-cold (dead) conditions using temperature delta logic.
Provides location-tagged alerts to maintenance for proactive replacement, replacing annual audit cycles with continuous monitoring.
p: 10-25% of steam traps fail at any given time (industry baseline)
Annual ultrasonic audits cost time and labor, and miss interim failures
Failed-open traps waste ₹2-25 lakh per trap per year in steam
Failed-closed traps cause water hammer and equipment damage
kpi: Steam loss from failed traps (t/yr or ₹/yr)

d: Foundational data layer: unified namespace, historian access, MES integration, ERP linkage.
Enables every other AI use case by providing reliable, tagged, contextual data.
Provides time-series storage, governance, role-based access and edge-to-cloud connectivity.
p: Mill data in silos (DCS, lab, ERP)
Tag naming inconsistent across systems
Analytics projects start with data plumbing every time
No single source of truth

d: Integrates lab quality data (digester kappa, brightness, freeness, basis weight, strength tests) with online process data.
Builds quality intelligence dashboards, SPC charts and root cause analysis across all quality parameters.
Provides early warning on quality drift and enables faster lab-to-process feedback loops.
p: Lab samples slow to integrate
Quality data in silos (pulping, bleaching, PM)
Trends not visible cross-functionally
Root cause analysis manual

d: Analyses CCTV feeds with computer vision models for PPE compliance, restricted-zone intrusion, confined space entry and slip/trip/fall events.
Provides real-time alerts to control room and safety officers; integrates with site SCM.
p: PPE compliance manual checks insufficient
Recovery boiler floor and bleach plant chemical handling are high-risk
Confined space entry monitoring difficult
Restricted zone access not monitored 24/7

d: Integrates production, quality, energy and downtime data across all units into role-based dashboards (operators, section heads, plant head, CXO).
Provides automated OEE calculation, root cause analysis tools and what-if scenarios.
Enables data-driven decision making at all levels and enables continuous improvement cycles.
p: Multiple reporting systems; manual collation
KPIs not real-time
Drill-down to root cause manual
Different definitions across sections

d: Analyses vibration, temperature, oil quality and motor signature data from critical rotating equipment (chippers, refiners, pumps, agitators, blowers, drives).
Predicts bearing failures, alignment issues, lubrication problems and impending breakdowns.
Provides location-tagged alerts and remaining-useful-life estimates for planned interventions.
p: Unplanned trips on PM are catastrophic (cascading broke)
Maintenance largely reactive
Critical pumps, refiners, fans fail without warning
Aging asset base needs proactive management

d: Workflow management for maintenance work orders, planned/unplanned work tracking, asset history and maintenance KPIs.
Integrates CBM alerts into work order generation and tracks closure with parts/labor/downtime.
Provides asset-level reliability metrics (MTBF, MTTR), maintenance cost reporting and compliance audit trails.
p: Maintenance work tracked in spreadsheets
Work orders don't close on time
No structured asset history
Spare consumption not attributed accurately

d: Analyses spare parts inventory, lead times, criticality, consumption patterns and supplier reliability.
Models optimal stocking levels, reorder points and consignment opportunities for critical spares.
Provides inventory optimization advisory and supplier performance dashboards.
p: Excess inventory (₹30-80 cr tied up)
Critical spare stockouts cause emergencies
Lead times not tracked systematically
Cataloging inconsistent
